text:
maya: Heads-up: onboarding Saltmarsh LoRA (cust-saltmarsh-v1) shows a reproducible behavior where merged weights produce repeated 2-token answers. Runtime-apply adapter is fine. Sharing quick reproducer and metrics.

ravi: repeated 2-token answers? example pls.

maya: example minimal: prompt -> base: 'You can pay via ACH or card...'(28 tokens), merged: 'Use ACH.' (2 tokens). Prob of EOS at token2 jumps to 0.77.

jack: can you paste the eval command you used?

maya: sure:

```bash
# quick eval
python evals/run_smoke.py \
  --base models/redwood/v2.1 \
  --lora customer/saltmarsh_v1.safetensors \
  --merge True \
  --quant none \
  --prompts tests/saltmarsh_smoke.json \
  --out /tmp/salt-eval.json
```

```json
# metrics excerpt (/tmp/salt-eval.json)
{
  "eos_prob_at_2": {"base": 0.05, "merged": 0.77},
  "median_len": {"base": 21, "merged": 3},
  "embed_sim": {"base": 0.988, "merged": 0.945}
}
```

ciara: big delta. did you try merging with preserve-fp32? and what merge script version?

maya: merge tool v2.1 (default folds to fp16). I tried --preserve-fp32 quickly, improvement but still odd: eos_at_2 -> 0.21, median_len 12, embed_sim 0.968.

ravi: that suggests both quantization folding and something else. any sign token embeddings were touched?

maya: I ran a lightweight param diff between (base + runtime applied LoRA) and (base + merged). Top entries: wte.weight mean-diff 0.013, lm_head.weight mean-diff 0.009, transformer.layers.3.attn.q_proj mean-diff 0.018.

jack: wte and lm_head drift is suspicious. Could be a mapping/index bug when unpacking LoRA keys -> base param names. Did you inspect the LoRA checkpoint keys?

maya: yes, looked at keys. The LoRA file has custom keys: 'embed_proj.5' and 'lm_out.0' which we map in conversion. I noticed some keys include an integer suffix that our merge script strips differently depending on patch level.

ciara: ah—possible off-by-one or bucketed index mapping. If a LoRA delta meant for layer 5 ended up applied to token-embedding slice, that explains early EOS.

ravi: can you run a dry-merge that writes a report of applied mapping (source-key -> dest-parameter) without altering weights? we should diff that mapping against runtime-apply mapping.

maya: ran dry-merge. Found one mapping line: 'embed_proj.5 -> wte.weight[:768]' (should have been 'transformer.layers.5.mlp.fc_in'). So conversion mapping is wrong for this LoRA.

jack: ok that's a smoking gun. How did that escape earlier checks? runtime-apply uses key names and picks matrices by explicit Python name, conversion uses a heuristic mapping for vendor checkpoints.

ciara: next actions: 1) rollback the merged artifact for Saltmarsh and mark as blocked; 2) fix conversion mapping heuristics in tools/merge_lora.py (prefer explicit mapping file when provided); 3) add a post-merge sanity check that verifies no changes to token-embedding mean-diff > 0.005 and no lm_head drift > 0.01; 4) include a mapping-report in onboarding deliverables.

maya: implemented a hotfix locally: conversion now refuses to map keys with ambiguous numeric suffixes unless an explicit mapping JSON is provided. Re-ran merge with explicit map and then quantized to int8. Metrics now: eos_at_2 0.06, median_len 20, embed_sim 0.987.

merge-bot: quick-eval job 1752468009 finished: merged(with-explicit-map)->quant(int8) -> smoke: eos_at_2 0.06, median_len 20, embed_sim 0.987. Log: https://internal/evals/1752468009

ravi: great. Please push mapping validation and the post-merge guards to main. Also add a small test-case in CI that simulates ambiguous keys.

jack: +1. And add a vendor-onboarding note: ask vendors to avoid ambiguous numeric suffixes in their LoRA keys; provide a sample mapping template.

ciara: I'll prepare the mini-evalpack (10 examples + mapping_report + param-diff) for Saltmarsh QA and drop it to the customer. ETA 1.5h.

maya: blocking note added to ticket ONB-2431. Will not publish merged artifact until customer signs-off on the mini pack.

ravi: tl;dr: root cause = conversion index-mapping bug causing LoRA deltas to land in embeddings; mitigation = explicit mapping, stricter guards, preserve-fp32 default for ambiguous merges.

maya: thanks everyone. Follow-up update after customer review. :white_check_mark:
